text:
Recent work supports combining content with interaction signals, but provides limited direct evidence for the exact constrained design: BERT4Rec with text and temporal features learned entirely from scratch. [CoCoRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12183) identifies a mismatch between textual similarity and collaborative transition patterns, using semantic codes and masked prediction objectives to bridge them. [WhitenRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10602) reports highly similar pretrained text embeddings across items, illustrating why broad semantic similarity can impair discrimination. These motivate retaining item IDs alongside content; their pretrained or ensemble components are unsuitable here.

Temporal conditioning has a clear precedent: [TiSASRec](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) incorporates pairwise time intervals alongside positions. Its temporal mechanism could inform a BERT4Rec attention bias without adopting its causal backbone. A suitable experimental hypothesis is one jointly trained network with ID embeddings plus gated title/description representations from a small, randomly initialized token encoder, and bucketed log-time gaps between observed interactions. Preserve numerals, units and model identifiers during tokenization; whether these improve specific-intent discrimination requires validation.

Keep [BERT4Rec’s masked-item objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690), hide target content whenever its ID is masked, and use appended-mask inference with the final nonpadding readout. Never supply a held-out target’s timestamp; temporal features must derive from available history. Compare content-only, time-only and combined modifications through separate single-model trials selected by macro validation HR@10. Compatibility and mood remain hypotheses, not observed labels.
